title: Video to specification: sam-3.1 tracking, muse-wonder-1.0 vs muse-spark-1.3 observations, muse-spark-1.3 specification (registration 2)
plan: Each seed: render the scripted demonstration (top + side), track with sam-3.1, rebuild the table-plane trace, compare with simulator ground truth per frame.
Both observation models see the same videos once each; their events are matched to ground-truth grasp/release events (same type and object, one-to-one, closest first).

Specification from the video trace (with the muse-spark-1.3 observations) vs specification from the ground-truth trace, both by muse-spark-1.3; compared by proposal signature (constraints not rejected: type, phase, selector, parameters; active goals: selector, target).
Every seed is reported, including failures.
metrics: object found rate (detection within 5 cm of ground truth, frames where visible)
table-plane centroid error (cm): median of per-object medians
grasp/release detection within 1 s and absolute timing error (s)
cup tilt error from the side view (deg)
proposal-signature equality, video vs ground-truth trace
observation models: event F1 at 0.5 s, relevant-object set correct, care cue for the cup when the demonstration kept it upright, latency

decision_rule.text: use muse-wonder-1.0 for observations only if its mean event F1 is at least 0.05 above muse-spark-1.3 and it gets the relevant-object set right at least as often; otherwise keep muse-spark-1.3

hypotheses: Tracking from rendered video meets every pre-stated threshold.
The specification from video has the same proposal signature as the one from the ground-truth trace on at least 18 of 20 seeds.
inputs_rule: for each seed: sample_layout(seed, 'eval'), the scripted demonstration, rendered by mirror.perception.render_demo_video (top + side), with its ground truth; all files listed with sha256 in inputs.json; no model call

threshold_scope.found_rate_min, centroid_cm_median_max,: perception estimates from sam-3.1 tracking and the reconstruction in mirror.perception; grasp/release times for these thresholds come from tracked object motion, never from the video models
threshold_scope.signature_equal_min: muse-spark-1.3 proposal from the video-derived trace (with the muse-spark-1.3 observations) vs from the ground-truth trace
threshold_scope.video models: muse-wonder-1.0 and muse-spark-1.3 observations have no pass/fail threshold; reported: event F1 at the published 0.5 s tolerance, mean absolute timing error of events matched within 2 s, relevant-object set, care cue, validator issues, latency and cost; the published decision rule (Wonder vs Spark) applies

observation.event_time: t_start of each reported grasp or release event
observation.matching: same event type and object kind, one-to-one, closest in time first

definitions.relevant_objects: among cup, block, marker and tray: the kit objects grasped in the demonstration plus the tray; a model is right when the kinds it marks relevant among these four equal that set
definitions.care_cue: a cue on the cup (or naming the cup) containing upright, level, vertical, tilt, spill or straight; expected when the cup's true tilt stayed below 15 degrees while it was held
definitions.tilt: the in-image tilt estimated from the side view vs the cup's true 3D tilt (only the in-image component is observable from one view); frames where the estimate is missing are not scored and are counted

render.function: mirror.perception.render_demo_video(scene, out_dir, cams=('top', 'side')) with the scripted teleoperation demonstration (same operator as the reference demonstration)
render.camera_settings: mirror.perception.cameras as frozen: top lookat (0, 0, 0), distance 1.30, azimuth 90, elevation -86, vertical field of view 45; side lookat (0, 0, 0.06), distance 1.75, azimuth 60, elevation -20, vertical field of view 45
render.overlays: none (no text, labels, paths or readouts)
render.machine: 8 NVIDIA L4 GPU compute boxes in parallel (4 CPU each, 2 to 3 seeds per box), EGL, image with pinned mujoco 3.17.0, numpy 2.4.6, scipy 1.17.1, imageio 2.38.1, pydantic 2.14.2 (the image of attempt 1); layouts sampled and ledgered here, rendered there from the saved scenes; GPU, driver, box count and package versions in versions.json, copied into inputs.json

tracking.frames: every 3rd frame of each 15 fps render, starting at frame 0, re-encoded once at the inputs stage and frozen by sha256 (bench_video.make_sam_copies); the video models watch the full 15 fps top video
tracking.procedure: mirror.perception.track.track_videos as frozen, on the 5 fps copies: per camera, three muse-spark-1.3 grounding calls on frame 0 (full frame for the table; a table crop for boxes and the visible ball count; one multi-image call of zoomed crops for cup, block and marker), then sam-3.1 box prompts: one video request (cup, block, marker, gripper) and one image request (table hypotheses, tray, wall) on frame 0
tracking.re_seeding: for gaps of at least 2 s in a moving object's track (at most 2 per camera, ranked: the other camera also missing it, then length), SAM tracks backwards over the gap from where the object is visible again (SAM's own box; no model call), or, when the gap runs to the end of the clip, from one muse-spark-1.3 grounding call on the last frame; one SAM video request per re-seed; merged only into missing frames and only if the seed mask is 0.3x to 3x the object's earlier median area; every re-seed is recorded and reported. Worst case per demonstration: 10 Spark calls and 8 SAM requests.
tracking.reconstruction: mirror.perception reconstruction as frozen (estimate, scene_from_video, trace_from_estimates), on the 5 fps tracks; scoring uses the ground-truth frames at the sampled times
tracking.five_fps_check: before this amendment, development demonstration 9001 was tracked live at 5 fps ($0.24): found rate 0.98, median centroid error cup 0.39 / block 0.58 / marker 0.90 cm, 5 of 6 events within 1 s, one re-seed; sim's 15 fps run of the same demonstration: block 2.46 cm, 5 of 6 within 1 s. Reconstruction from every 3rd frame of the 15 fps tracks gave the same centroid errors. Fewer frames carry a cup tilt estimate at 5 fps (59 vs 168 sampled).

observation_runs: one muse-wonder-1.0 and one muse-spark-1.3 observation per seed, no repeats
spend_rule: all model calls of this registration (grounding, SAM, re-seeds, observations, proposals; every attempt, including calls of seeds interrupted by a restart) count against the dollar cap, read from the clients' usage logs. Seeds run 8 at a time. Before a seed starts: projected = mean measured cost of finished full seeds (spend_projection_per_seed_usd until one exists); if spent + reservations of running seeds + 1.5 x projected > cap, the seed runs without muse-wonder-1.0 when 1.5 x (projected - Wonder) fits; otherwise no further seed starts, running seeds finish, and the remaining seeds are listed as not run. Tracking is never dropped.
budget_note: Request counts are bookkeeping only (still counted and reported); the dollar cap is the binding limit. This changes a resource limit only; no threshold, metric, seed or decision rule changes.

spec_comparison.pass_fail: the published strict proposal signature (signature_equal_min = 18 of 20), unchanged
spec_comparison.reported_only: same structure ignoring numeric limits (items, phases, selectors and parameter names equal; numbers may differ), with every numeric difference listed per seed (for example a cup tilt limit of 10 vs 15 degrees); not a pass/fail measure, added before any input exists

development_status: perception was tuned on the reference demonstration and development seeds 9001 and 9002 only. On dev 9002 it still misses the marker's grasp and release (3 of 6 events; the marker's carry is reconstructed wrongly) and its strict signature differs offline. Nothing in the design was loosened after these development results.
disclosures: camera intrinsics known (45 degree vertical field of view); table size known (1.2 x 1.0 m); object, tray and wall-thickness sizes from the kit catalogue
the camera is assumed to be on the operator's (-y) side of the table, which resolves the table rectangle's symmetry
the bead count is the number of balls visible to the grounding model, not the true count
the gripper opening is not observed: closed while an object is carried, open otherwise
cup tilt only where the cup is clearly visible in the side view (visibility, occlusion and temporal consistency gates), from an in-image silhouette fit
the render look was adjusted for segmentation (soft wood grain, dark floor, opaque walls)
perception was tuned on the reference demonstration and dev 9001/9002; evaluation seeds were never rendered or sampled by the perception track
SAM 3.1 noun-phrase prompts alone found only the blue cube, the table (top) and the wall (side) on these renders, so muse-spark-1.3 grounding seeds box prompts
static scene parts are segmented once on frame 0 and held
one-view frames: resting objects are placed on their support; carried objects hidden under the gripper follow it; gripper depth from apparent size
rendered video, not camera footage, rendered on an NVIDIA L4 with EGL
registration 2: attempt 1 on seeds 70000-70019 failed for a harness reason and is reported in results/eval_video/ATTEMPT_1.md; its 12 tracked seeds are not used
seeds run in parallel (8 at a time) and the tracking latency reported per seed includes waiting for the shared CPU; results do not depend on the order

supersedes.outcome: attempt 1 did not produce a result: results/eval_video/ATTEMPT_1.md

rationale: Attempt 1 of registration 'video' failed for a harness reason: the runner passed the whole observation block of the design to observe() as keyword arguments, so every video-model call raised TypeError before any request; the specification was then proposed without observations, which is not the registered condition; and the run stopped after 12 of 20 seeds when the machine restarted, with no way to resume. A frozen registration cannot be patched, so this registration repeats the design on 20 new seeds with three harness changes: only the arguments observe() declares are passed (tested against the real function), finished seeds are checkpointed and a restarted run resumes, and seeds run four at a time under a spend reservation. Everything measured and every threshold, tolerance, metric and decision rule is the same as registration 'video' with its amendments 1 and 2 (hashes in 'supersedes'). Attempt 1's tracking outputs (seeds 70000-70011) were not summarised before this design was written.
observation_call: observe(top video, model, client, strategy='video'): of the observation block only the names that observe() declares in its signature are passed (bench_video.observe_kwargs); camera, event_time and matching are descriptive and used by the scorer
spend_projection_note: from measured calls before this design: attempt 1 tracking on 12 seeds (sam-3.1 $2.93, muse-spark-1.3 grounding $0.82), one muse-wonder-1.0 observation of the 82 s reference clip ($0.20), and the development rehearsal of this harness (8 truncated demos, 8 workers, $0.26 per seed without Wonder, no HTTP 429)
resume_rule: each finished seed (completed or failed) is written to seeds/<seed>.json next to the ledger. A restarted run skips those seeds and runs the others; a seed that had started without finishing is run again from the start and listed in the report. A finished seed is never run twice. The report states every attempt and restart.
